items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: You see on piano we had Louis Russell on piano, and banjo, Willie Foster, that's Pop Foster's brother, on banjo.

ctx.x: Well I'll give you a few of them. You see on piano we had Louis Russell on piano, and banjo, Willie Foster, that's Pop Foster's brother, on banjo. On drums we had Paul Barbaran on drums. And on bass we had a bass player called Buford. Now on trumpet we had King Oliver, Red Island, so far back I can't think of the boy's name. Yeah. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I…
Great kind of guy. Darnell Harris?

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: It was Red Allen, Willie Foster, and me. We joined the King Oliver Band in St. Louis.

ctx.x: St. Louis, Missouri. It was Red Allen, Willie Foster, and me. We joined the King Oliver Band in St. Louis. Everybody left from St. Louis to New York. He played in the Savoy Ballroom. What kind of fellow was he, Josephine?
And what did he like to do? Strictly business. Everything on a business basis, huh?

items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: And the ones who left here together was Willie Foster, Red Allen, and myself. See, we left together and we went to St. Louis.

ctx.x: Where was he when he located you then? He was in Chicago.

In Chicago. Yeah, King Oliver was in Chicago. But I didn't meet him in Chicago. He left Chicago. He was going on a job in New York. But we met him in St. Louis. St. Louis. And the ones who left here together was Willie Foster, Red Allen, and myself. See, we left together and we went to St. Louis. Willie Foster is Pop Foster's brother.
Yes, we talked to him up and he's in Baton Rouge. We saw him last January. Last January.

items.title: Willie Foster Interview
items.q: We left New Orleans together to go to St. Burst and George to kill Oliver.

ctx.x: Oh, no. No, don't worry about that.
But we left New Orleans, a little red alley. And the fellow named Paul. Paul Barnes.
Paul Barnes, yes. He's in California. He was back home though for about two months in the fall. He played there.
